Dear Colleague,

I saw David Meyer in consultation on January 03, 2025. This visit was prompted by the patient's recent episode of a urinary tract infection, which appears to be adequately controlled as of now. His blood pressure at this visit was 134/63, and his weight was recorded at 163 pounds.

Regarding Mr. Meyer's Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) with systemic organ involvement, his condition is currently well-controlled. He is on a regimen that includes mycophenolate 500 mg and belimumab 200 mg injections. There have been no recent flares or complications associated with his SLE, and he continues to follow up regularly to monitor his condition.

In reference to Mr. Meyer’s Parkinson’s disease, which began at the age of 48, it is also currently controlled. He has been taking pramipexole 0.5 mg as his medication, which has been effective in managing his symptoms. There are no current signs of progression or severe side effects from his treatment.

Furthermore, the patient has recently been treated for a urinary tract infection (UTI). He was prescribed sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim 800/160 mg, and the infection appears to be under control with no further complications. His urinalysis results from this visit were normal, indicating no ongoing infection.

During the consultation, I noted Mr. Meyer’s social history. He currently smokes cigarettes, consuming one pack per day, which he has been doing since 1986. His alcohol consumption is approximately six drinks per week. He has been honest and forthcoming about these habits, which we have discussed in detail.

In terms of physical examination, Mr. Meyer's general appearance is unremarkable. His vital signs, aside from the blood pressure and weight, were within normal limits. His neurological examination revealed no new abnormalities, consistent with the controlled status of his Parkinson's disease. The musculoskeletal examination was also within normal limits with no signs of SLE activity.

Given the stable nature of his conditions, my recommendations are to continue with the current medications and to maintain regular follow-up appointments to monitor his health status. It is crucial for Mr. Meyer to continue adhering to his treatment regimens and to monitor for any signs of disease flare-ups or complications.

Thank you for this referral. Please do not hesitate to reach out if Mr. Meyer requires any further evaluation or if there are any changes in his health status.

Sincerely,

Dr. Steven Campbell
Family Medicine
